drivingQuestion: How should the mishna's question about dipping be worded?
outcomeNote: Rava's emendation replaces the mishna wording

segments.he: מָה נִשְׁתַּנָּה הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה מִכׇּל הַלֵּילוֹת, שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אָנוּ מַטְבִּילִין פַּעַם אֶחָת, הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה — שְׁתֵּי פְעָמִים. מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא: אַטּוּ כׇּל יוֹמָא לָא סַגִּיא דְּלָא מְטַבְּלָא חֲדָא זִימְנָא? אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, הָכִי קָתָנֵי: שֶׁבְּכָל הַלֵּילוֹת אֵין אָנוּ חַיָּיבִין לְטַבֵּל אֲפִילּוּ פַּעַם אֶחָת, הַלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה — שְׁתֵּי פְעָמִים.
segments.en: The mishna states that one of the questions is: «Why is this night different from all other nights? As on all other nights we dip once;» however, «on this night» we dip «twice. Rava strongly objects to this» statement of the mishna: «Is that to say» that on «every» other «day there is no alternative» but to «dip once?» Is there an obligation to dip at all on other days, as indicated by the wording of the mishna? «Rather, Rava said» that «this is what» the mishna «is teaching: As on all other nights we are not obligated to dip even once;» however, «on this night» we are obligated to dip «twice.»
